elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1 chapeau: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ('Sanofi Indemnitees')" — express defence duty running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 14.1 chapeau covers "any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement" in favour of the Sanofi Indemnitees (Sanofi and its Affiliates); "Third Party Claims" is defined at 1.126.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb (d): "any allegation that the services performed or deliverables provided by RevMed under this Agreement or the RevMed Licensed Technology infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights of any Third Party". The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" returned false, but that reflects the pre-redline text (the basis for the deviation call); the rendered operative language plainly supplies the limb.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New limb (e): "RevMed's breach of Applicable Law"; "Applicable Law" is a defined term used elsewhere in the Agreement (rationale cites Section 1.8).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb (f): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sanofi's Confidential Information or other data of Sanofi caused by RevMed" — Vendor-caused breach of Customer data, not limited to selected data types.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — simple negligence a fortiori captures gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is express.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.3(a) Notice of Claim: "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an 'Indemnification Claim Notice')", with a favourable prejudice-only qualifier retained.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim ... by giving written notice to the Indemnified Party within [***]".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.3(e) Cooperation: Indemnified Party "will cooperate in the defense thereof and will furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested", with Vendor reimbursement of out-of-pocket costs retained.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 14.2 as amended reads only "(a) content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law", with the former Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization, warranty-breach and obligation-breach limbs struck as "[Intentionally omitted]".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same new 14.1(d) infringement/misappropriation limb, running to the Sanofi Indemnitees for Third Party Claims.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification carve-out was added, which is more favourable to Customer than the fallback permits; the condition therefore does not bite.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination carve-out added; only the retained Sanofi-fault exceptions ((i)-(iii)) apply, which is within (indeed narrower than) what the fallback tolerates.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no Customer-specification carve-out added; absence is Customer-favourable and does not defeat the level.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in amended 14.1-14.3; the redline adds only the indemnity limb.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic is present in the rendered language.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is inserted; the indemnity remains uncapped under Section 14.5, which the drafter deliberately preserved as more favourable.

elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: (Cross-level note) The retained "indemnify, defend and hold harmless" chapeau also underpins the fallback IP indemnity.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are met on the face of the rendered language — the retained 14.1 chapeau supplies defence/indemnity for Customer and Affiliates against Third Party Claims, retained (a) supplies negligence/wilful misconduct, new limbs (d)-(f) supply IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law and Vendor-caused data breach, retained 14.3(a)/(b)/(e) supply notice, control of defence and cooperation, and 14.2 is narrowed to Customer-provided content plus Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

The deterministic check 'vendor indemnity for IP infringement present' = false does not defeat the finding: inspected in substance, the rendered clause contains an express allegation-of-infringement/misappropriation limb at 14.1(d); the failed check corresponds to the pre-redline text and in fact corroborates the deviation call (no Vendor IP indemnity existed, i.e. walk-away territory).

Fallback is not complete (no procure/modify/replace, no refund, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is met and, as the rationale notes, importing the super-cap would cap an indemnity that is presently uncapped under Section 14.5 — declining it is Customer-favourable.

Minimality holds: the only additions are the three indemnity limbs required by the checklist and the narrowing of Customer's own indemnity; no survival tail, expense language, extra damages categories or boilerplate was added, and 14.1(a)-(c) plus the whole of 14.3 are retained verbatim.

Voluntary concession to note (not a minimality failure but repairable): conforming the exception chapeau from the original limb range to '((a) through (f))' extends the Sanofi-fault carve-outs (i)-(iii) to the new IP, breach-of-law and data-breach limbs. That was not required by any element; leaving the chapeau tied to the original limbs would keep the new limbs carve-out-free and is the better Customer outcome if RevMed pushes back elsewhere.

Drafting clean-up before sending: 14.2 now reads '(b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law; or (c) [Intentionally omitted]; or (d) [Intentionally omitted];' — delete the trailing 'or' after (b) and the vestigial placeholders (and the stray '71' page artifact) so the list closes cleanly on (b).

Verify the two definitional anchors in the inserted text: 'RevMed Licensed Technology' (cited as Section 1.99) and 'Applicable Law' (cited as Section 1.8) are not in the resolved-definitions set supplied here. If either is not a defined term in the executed text, limb (d)/(e) would leave an undefined term; confirm the cross-references before circulating.

Intent is preserved: limb (d) is confined to RevMed's services, deliverables and RevMed Licensed Technology and does not reach Sanofi's downstream Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization, so it does not convert into a freedom-to-operate indemnity or contradict the Article X infringement machinery or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement; the Section 13.5 non-infringement warranty disclaimer is not contradicted because an indemnity is a separate risk allocation from a warranty.
